record.original_question: For integer sequences a1(n), ..., aℓ(n), are the following conditions equivalent: (i) the sequences are good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations; (ii) they are good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. If (a1(n)), . . . ,(aℓ(n)) are sequences of integers, then show that the following statements are equivalent: • The sequences (a1(n)), . . . ,(aℓ(n)) are good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations. • The sequences (a1(n)), . . . ,(aℓ(n)) are good for ℓ-convergence of ℓ-step nilsystems. • The sequence (1/N) Σ ψ(a1(n), . . . , aℓ(n)) converges for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ-variables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer ℓ ≥ 1. Throughout, "system" means an invertible measure-preserving system (X, ℬ, μ, T₁, …, T_ℓ) consisting of a probability space and ℓ commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations.

An ℓ-step nilsystem is a system of the form (G/Γ, T_{b_1}, …, T_{b_ℓ}), where G is an ℓ-step nilpotent Lie group, Γ ⊂ G is a discrete cocompact subgroup, b_1, …, b_ℓ ∈ G commute, and T_{b_i}(xΓ) = b_i x Γ; the measure is the Haar measure on G/Γ.

A basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence in ℓ variables is a sequence of the form ψ(n_1, …, n_ℓ) = F(b_1^{n_1} ⋯ b_ℓ^{n_ℓ} Γ), where G/Γ is an ℓ-step nilmanifold, b_1, …, b_ℓ ∈ G commute, and F : G/Γ → ℂ is continuous.

Let a_1(n), …, a_ℓ(n) be sequences of integers. Say that (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations if for every system (X, ℬ, μ, T_1, …, T_ℓ) with T_1, …, T_ℓ commuting and every f_1, …, f_ℓ ∈ L^∞(μ), the averages
   (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N (T_1^{a_1(n)} f_1) ⋯ (T_ℓ^{a_ℓ(n)} f_ℓ)
converge in L²(μ) as N → ∞.

Say that (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems if the same convergence holds whenever (X, ℬ, μ, T_1, …, T_ℓ) is an ℓ-step nilsystem and f_1, …, f_ℓ are continuous.

Prove or disprove that the following three statements are equivalent:
(i) (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations;
(ii) (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems;
(iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a_1(n), …, a_ℓ(n)) converge as N → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns equivalence of three notions of being "good for ℓ-convergence" for integer sequences in the setting of commuting transformations and ℓ-step nilsystems. Subsequent work by Frantzikinakis and collaborators (e.g., on multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences, arXiv:1407.0631) addresses related decompositions and weighted convergence questions, but I could not locate a definitive resolution of the three-way equivalence as stated. Status appears unresolved in the literature I was able to verify.

status_evidence.title: Multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiple correlation sequences for commuting transformations and their decomposition as nilsequence plus error term.
status_evidence.claim: Related work develops the structural connection between commuting-transformation averages and nilsequences but does not explicitly settle the stated three-way equivalence.
